title: OSD firmware descriptor 0.7
description: A firmware, mod, module, application, script or extension a device can run (the `kind`): who makes it, where it lives, its licence, what it changes to the device's MIDI, and how it is installed. It points to the author's own release; it never carries the firmware itself.

^_.description: A note for people; never read by a program.

kind.description: What the descriptor is. `firmware`: a stock firmware, the one a device ships with or a vendor releases. `mod`: a whole modified firmware, installed in place of a stock one. `module`: a plug-in applied to a stock firmware, one among several an assembly stacks. `application`: a program installed on the host system of a device. `script`: a script a device runs. `extension`: any other thing a device can run.

descriptor.description: The OSD device descriptor it is for (maker/file, e.g. korg/minilogue).

^_.description: A note for people; never read by a program.

device.description: The device it is made for.

descriptor.description: The OSD device descriptor of its MIDI.

same_as.description: When it answers to another firmware's MIDI unchanged, that descriptor.

changes.description: What it adds or changes, in words.

^_.description: A note for people; never read by a program.

midi.description: What the firmware understands over MIDI on this device.

^_.description: A note for people; never read by a program.

based_on.description: The lineage: the firmware the target is forked or built from, one version. It says nothing of what the target runs on.

^_.description: A note for people; never read by a program.

targets.description: The devices it is made for. Each target carries its own MIDI, its lineage (based_on) and what it runs on (runs_on).

^_.description: A note for people; never read by a program.

items.description: A person or group, as they sign.

^_.description: A note for people; never read by a program.

release.description: Where this version is downloaded, from its author.

license.description: An SPDX licence id (CC-BY-4.0, CC0-1.0, MIT…), public-domain, NOASSERTION (SPDX: the source states no licence; nothing is asserted) or NONE (SPDX: the source declares that it grants no licence). SPDX's two special values are written in capitals; other spellings are refused.

identify.description: How the device shows which firmware it runs (its identity reply, a screen).

revert.description: How to go back to the maker's firmware.

^_.description: A note for people; never read by a program.
A note for people; never read by a program.

builder.description: The tool that makes the assembly from the stock OS and modules, which the person flashes (Elekloader, Modwerk). It stays the reference for building, installing and updating the module; OSD never rehosts.

^_.description: A note for people; never read by a program.

version.description: A version that is compared: components separated by one dot, each a number then optional letters. A version outside this grammar is only displayed, and compared it answers unknown. Versions compare component by component (split on `.`): a number, then optional letters without case; 1.40 < 1.40B < 1.40C < 1.41, 1.9 < 1.10, 1.40 = 1.40.0.

versions.description: The base versions the target runs on: an explicit list, or a range whose bounds are included (a min alone is open upward, a max alone downward). Absent, a version fits the target unknown: neither yes nor no.

^_.description: A note for people; never read by a program.
A note for people; never read by a program.

runs_on.description: The base firmware a target runs on, and its versions; no versions leaves "does this version fit" unknown.
